title: SAT Session Learning Report & Learner Model Update (Session cf15003d-c6f5-438c-bf0f-fdb24d8a5841)
executiveSummary: During the initial diagnostic session (cf15003d-c6f5-438c-bf0f-fdb24d8a5841), the learner achieved a perfect score of 12/12 (100% accuracy) across 11 Reading and Writing items and 1 Math item, all at difficulty level 2. Total session elapsed time was 3 minutes and 47 seconds, with an overall average pacing of 17 seconds per item (well below the target average of 60 seconds). A primary psychological pattern emerged: under-confidence. Despite zero errors, the learner flagged 7 out of 12 items as 'unsure' (6) or 'guessing' (1). Because all items were tested at difficulty level 2 with a single question per skill in one session, no skill can yet be classified as fully mastered, fluent, or retained. The primary recommendation is to escalate difficulty to Level 3 while reinforcing rule-based confidence self-trust.

limitations: Single session observation (cf15003d-c6f5-438c-bf0f-fdb24d8a5841) covering only 12 items.
Only 1 item tested per skill; retention and multi-form transfer cannot be verified yet (requires >= 3 attempts across >= 2 sessions).
All items were at difficulty level 2; ceiling effect prevents assessing performance on high-difficulty (Level 3-4) questions.
Math domain representation is limited to a single linear equation item (0f1269e1-405a-4f00-b38f-e5c86f16f23b).

confidenceCalibration.claim: The learner demonstrates significant under-confidence / conservative self-assessment: 7 of 12 items (58.3%) were marked as 'unsure' (6 items) or 'guessing' (1 item), despite achieving 100% accuracy on all of them in fast execution times.
High confidence strongly correlates with high speed: items marked 'confident' averaged 15 seconds per item compared to 18 seconds for 'unsure'/'guessing' items.
